_note: v2 hooks for the Palais de justice (B14_tribunal), Oct 31 2026 batch 7: the tribunal room moved here from the Musée with its painting, hooks and cards (see docs/changes/RELOCATIONS_REWORK.tsv).

fr_injure_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a fussy lady juror in a feathered hat leaning out of the jury box and wagging her finger at a startled lawyer in a white wig. Moved from the wall-text room R_text_crime_01 (where it was only a blank plaque) into this painted room. Gate 29 false-friend note.
fr_injure_noun.note: An insult, not an injury (an injury is une blessure).

fr_criminalite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a cartoon criminal in a striped shirt, eye mask and cap sitting on a bench sipping tea from a dented tin mug.

fr_brutalite_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a big hairy cartoon brute looking sheepish over a china teapot and a smashed teacup on the floor.

fr_penal_adj.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a cartoon jailbird in striped clothes signing a paper at a little desk with an enormous feather quill pen.
fr_penal_adj.note: A legal word with a serious, negative ring.

fr_racket_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a cartoon mafioso in a pinstripe suit and fedora proudly holding a tennis racket and a ball. Gate 29 false-friend note.
fr_racket_noun.note: Extortion, often bullying kids for money at school; not a tennis racket (that is une raquette).

fr_scelerat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a big stalk of celery with a cartoon face in a black eye mask, striped shirt and flat cap sitting in the dock.
fr_scelerat_noun.note: A strong, old-fashioned word for a wicked person.

fr_cambriolage_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a sneaky masked burglar tiptoeing away with an enormous wedge of brie cheese.

fr_revolver_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): a glass display case on a pedestal with a small antique revolver lying on a turning round stand. Moved from the wall-text room R_text_crime_01 (where it was only a blank plaque) into this painted room.

fr_affut_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/tribunal (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to tribunal/tribunal in batch 7, painting kept): three spectators leaning over the upper balcony railing, peering through opera glasses. Gate 29 second sense.
fr_affut_noun.note: Mostly in être à l'affût = to be on the lookout; also an old cannon's gun carriage.
